scenario.description: A district curriculum director must approve the purchasing and deployment plan for a high-school digital music production lab, with input from a music teacher, an instructional technology specialist, and a business-office manager.

shared_context.S1: The high school has submitted a proposal for a digital music production lab serving an introductory music technology course.
shared_context.S2: The draft proposal requests 10 laptops, a commercial cloud music platform, $8,000 from the general fund, and installation on September 1, 2026.
shared_context.S3: Dr. Monroe has final approval authority for the equipment, funding, software, and deployment plan.
shared_context.S4: At the weekly capital-request meeting, Dr. Monroe routinely asks the requesting teacher, instructional technology specialist, and business-office manager to report any relevant findings before approval.
shared_context.S5: The capital-request meeting's final approval is based on the findings reported during that meeting; once the three requested reports are heard, Dr. Monroe records the revised quantities, approved platform, funding terms, deadlines, installation date, and required documentation without waiting for additional pricing research or follow-up estimates.

PF1.text: Ms. Patel's classroom trial with the enrolled section showed that all 12 students need simultaneous stations, with one laptop and one USB microphone per student; she completed the trial this week and recorded the results in her classroom planning log, but the log was not attached to the capital request.

PF2.text: Mr. Lawson's completed network and privacy review found that the commercial cloud platform cannot be used with student accounts; the district-managed SoundLab EDU platform is approved and requires managed student accounts plus a security configuration record. He closed the technology review ticket this week, but it has not yet been linked to the purchasing request.

PF3.text: Ms. Green confirmed that the Arts Innovation Grant will fund this project, but only up to exactly $6,800 and only if the purchase order is issued by August 20, 2026. Under the grant's purchasing sequence, the purchase order must be followed by procurement and setup, making September 15, 2026 the earliest feasible installation date. She received the grant award notice this week and filed it in the business-office grant folder, but the funding note has not been added to the proposal.

acceptance_conditions: The lab must provide 12 laptops so all enrolled students can work simultaneously.
The lab must provide 12 USB microphones, one for each student station.
The district-managed SoundLab EDU platform must be selected.
The Arts Innovation Grant must be the sole funding source.
The approved budget must be exactly $6,800.
The purchase order must be issued by August 20, 2026.
Installation must be scheduled for September 15, 2026.
A dedicated security configuration record commitment must be included.
A grant-compliant purchase-order commitment must be included.
The teacher's station-capacity finding must be cited in the justification.

content_checks.C8: 'PF2' in credited_facts and any(c['type'] == 'documentation' and c['target'] == 'Mr. Lawson' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: 'PF3' in credited_facts and any(c['type'] == 'documentation' and c['target'] == 'Ms. Green' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The classroom trial changes the equipment quantities from the draft's 10 laptops and no listed microphones to exactly 12 laptops and 12 USB microphones, and supplies the finding that must be cited.
The technology review changes the software choice to SoundLab EDU and requires a dedicated security configuration record for managed student accounts.

The grant notice changes the sole funding source to the Arts Innovation Grant, fixes the budget at exactly $6,800, requires the purchase order by 2026-08-20, and identifies 2026-09-15 as the earliest feasible installation date after procurement and setup.
